info Attachments can be added to assets or users. Below demonstrates how to add an attachment to any item. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen if anything is displayed. Type ‘118’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® displays the item ‘7/16 Deep Socket’. Navigate to the ‘Attachments’ tab (located below the Item Serial Number). Press ‘Add Attachment to Barcode’. Navigate to any appropriate Attachment, then press ‘Open’. ➤ This will add an Attachment to this specific Barcode Id. On the ‘Attachments’ tab, select ‘Add Attachment to Part Number’. Navigate to the appropriate Attachment, then press ‘Open’. ➤ This will add an Attachment to this specific Part Number. ➤ If another item has the same Part Number, then the Attachment will cascade to that Item. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen. Type ‘118’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® displays item ‘7/16 Deep Socket’. Navigate to the ‘Attachments’ tab (located below the Item Serial Number). Verify the Attachments saved to the ‘Barcode Id’ section and the ‘Part Number’ section. ➤ By double clicking on the specific Attachment, it will open the file.

info There are numerous ways to add items within TCMax®. The easiest ways to add items within TCMax® are to simply enter or scan the Barcode Id directly from the Main Screen. Type ‘100’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “New Item”. ➤ If you are adding Items to the ‘TCMax® Demo Shop’ for the first time, the following message will appear, press ‘OK’ through the message. Enter the item information you wish to have for this item. Press the ‘F5’ key to save the item or press ‘Save’. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Adding a new User can easily be done directly from the Main Screen of TCMax® within seconds by simply scanning or entering the User Id in the Input Box. Type ‘33’ in the Main Input box press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says New User. Type a ‘Name’ in the Username box then press ‘Save’. ➤ Your User is now created, and you can issue items to that User. Press ‘Esc’ to clear the Main Screen. Type ‘33’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 900’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘117’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Items with overdue calibration can be issued to users with the Allow Override Constraint permission. Type ‘06’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 72’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘114’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Overdue Calibration” and the message reads “Item Not Issued”. [Demonstrate the ability to change a calibration due date easily] Press the ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen. Type ‘114’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, the overdue Torque Wrench is displayed. Click in the Calibration Due Date box. Press ‘T’ for today. Press ‘Y’ to add years. Press ‘M’ to add months. Press ‘+ OR -’ to add or subtract days. Press the ‘Enter’ key to save the updated calibration date. ➤ After the Calibration Due Date has been updated, you will be able issue the item as long as it is no longer Overdue. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Below you will find an example of a User trying to issue an item they are NOT certified to take, along with an example of certifying the User for that item and completing the issue process. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 1200’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘704’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says "User Not Certified". ➤ This item will not be issued because the User is not certified to take this item. Adjust your Mode from ‘Mode = Issue/Turn-In’ to ‘Mode = Training Completion’. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘7004’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says "Completed". ➤ The User will now be certified to take the Wire Welder with the Barcode ID, 704. Adjust your Mode from ‘Mode = Training Completion’ to ‘Mode = Issue/Turn-In’. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 1200’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘704’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says "Issued". ➤ You will now see that the User is certified to issue the item. ➤ Certifications can also be assigned from the Main Screen from the Certified User tab. The example provided above is an example of how our Course Feature is used to certify a User. ➤ An unlimited number of Certifications can be added to a User, granting permissions to an unlimited number of Part Numbers with a single barcode scan.

info The TCMax® Dashboard was designed to help a supervisor, manager, etc. quickly and visually monitor the status of many of their items, users, and courses all from a single display. The blue line running along the right-hand side of the Main Screen is used to open the Dashboard. ➤ ‘Left click’ on the blue line to fully open the Dashboard. ‘Right click’ on the blue line to partially open the Dashboard. ‘Left click’ on the blue line to fully open the Dashboard. With the Dashboard opened, you will see different Categories in blue. With the Categories expanded, you will see your Subcategories. Select the ‘Overdue Item Calibrations’ Subcategory under the ‘Calibration Status’ Category, you will notice a table with the information for that Subcategory will appear. You can send this table to Excel if it is something you need to save or share. To close the table, simply press ‘Close’ or press ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner. This will take you back to the Dashboard. ➤ Within the TCMax® Dashboard, different Categories can be moved around. Press and hold the ‘Kit Status’ Category. ‘Drag’ this to the top left, above the ‘Current Issue Status’ Category. You will notice the Kit Status was rearranged to appear as the very first Status. ‘Right’ click on the blue line now running along the left-hand side of the screen. This will show you the Dashboard in a mini pane along with the Main Screen. ➤ The mini pane will only show the left column of the Dashboard. ➤ This is useful if you need to move status headers to the left side and keep them open in a mini pane to monitor, while completing actions on the Main Screen within TCMax®. ‘Right’ click on the blue line again to close the Dashboard.

info The Database Maintenance screen is used to create Backups of your Database (if connected locally), Change Database Connections, restore to TCMax® Demo Data, Migrate Special Options used in TCMax® Version 8, Delete Logs and Rebuild Indexes, Delete Sites and Shop Codes, activate Asset History Tracking, and enable Auto Load Presets per Shop Code. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘File’ then select ‘Database Maintenance’ . TCMax® says “Enter User Id”. Type ‘01’ in the User Id box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Enter Password”. Type ‘01’ in the User Password box then press the ‘Enter’ key. ➤ If connected locally, you will notice 9 (nine) different tabs starting with Backup Database. If connected through a Microsoft SQL Server® then you will notice 8 (eight) different tabs starting with Change Database Connections. To close Database Maintenance press ‘Close’.

info There are four different inventory modes to help you record your sessions and conditions of your assets. The following demonstrates the Physical (Kit) Inventory mode. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Tools’ then select ‘Inventory’ or press ‘Ctrl+Shift+I’ on your keyboard from the Main Screen to enter the Inventory Selection screen. Select ‘Physical Inventory’. From Step 1, select ‘Full’ for the type of Inventory being performed. From Step 2, select ‘Children’ for the generation level. From Step 3, verify ‘TCMax® Demo Shop’ is selected. From Step 4, type ‘121’ and press the ‘Enter’ key. With your focus in the Inventory screen, type ‘521’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. ➤ The inventory screen does not have an input box, but as long as your cursor is focused within the screen then you will be able to enter the appropriate Barcode Id of the item you wish to inventory. Type ‘522’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘523’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘524’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Enter Quantity”. Notice that TCMax® shows you that there are “20” Steel Carbiners that should be in the Pumper Truck by displaying a “20” on the screen. If any are missing from your actual count then you would want to adjust the Inventoried Quantity to show what is physically there. Adjust this quantity to '19' and press the 'Enter' key, TCMax® says “Discrepancy”. ➤ You will notice that the Item will appear under the Discrepancy List and display a Discrepancy Type of 'Quantity Did Not Match'. Type ‘16’ under Inventoried Quantity then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® will display a 'No Item Found' popup. This is showing the item does not exist. Press 'OK' on the popup. Type ‘525’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘526’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘527’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘121’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Pretend you find one more item (that does not belong in the Pumper Truck, 121). Type ‘007’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Discrepancy”. ➤ You will notice that the Item that was entered will appear from the Discrepancy List and display a Discrepancy Type of ‘Does Not Belong To This Inventory’. From the Discrepancy List, click on the ‘Information Tool Tip’ directly next to the 1/4 Deep Socket 3/8 Item Name. ➤ This will show information about the item including what Kit this item belongs to. Select the Discrepancy for the 1/4 Deep Socket 3/8 then select ‘Resolve’. ➤ After selecting resolve TCMax® will provide a ‘Resolve Discrepancy’ screen where you can enter the action that was taken to resolve the discrepancy, if you cancel out of this screen then it will be listed as a discrepancy for the Inventory of Item 121. Enter the action that was taken to resolve the discrepancy then select ‘Accept’. Select ‘Complete Inventory’ at the bottom of the screen. The Physical Inventory will now be completed, press ‘Close’ to exit the ‘Physical Inventory Setup’ screen and ‘Inventory Selection’ screen.

info Items with the ‘No Turn-In’ box checked are considered Expendable Items. When checking this box, it automatically checks the ‘Multiple items with this same barcode number’ box. Items with the ‘Issue multiple of this item with single scan’ box checked causes TCMax® to ask how many of these items you wish to take. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 99’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘702’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Enter Quantity”. Type ‘6’ in the Multi-Item Issue box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue” and the ‘Quantity On Hand’ and ‘Quantity Available’ on the Main Screen decreases by two. If your ‘Quantity On Hand’ of this item goes below the “Reorder Qty” then TCMax® will announce “Attention” to tell you that you need to reorder this item. ➤ Your Expendable Items issued will only appear under the Users Expendables tab when a User is displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info If a Work Location won't be used in your environment, this prompt can be turned off within Options. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 127’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘003’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Type ‘005’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Type ‘006’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Type ‘605’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Overdue Calibration” but does not say Issue. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Items without the ‘No Turn-In’ box checked are considered Non-Expendable Items. These are items that are expected to be returned. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 56’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘116’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. ➤ The ‘Quantity On Hand’ remains the same since this item will eventually be returned. The ‘Quantity Available’ on the Main Screen decreases by one. ➤ Non-expendable items are not just single quantity items, they can also have multiple of an item with the same barcode number depending on the way they are setup in TCMax®. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Rags are an item that has its own Item Type. This allows for TCMax® to recognize these item types as an item that goes through the laundry process before returning to stock. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 78’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “‘Enter’ Quantity”. Type ‘2’ in the Multi-item Issue box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. ➤ The ‘Quantity On Hand’ remains the same since this will be returned eventually. The ‘Quantity Available’ on the Main Screen decreases by two. Also, the Rags appear in the list of issued items. Type ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key (as if you are turning them in), TCMax® says “Enter Quantity”. ➤ You will notice you can issue more out at the bottom, or you can select other options before turning in the Rags. In ‘Step 2: Select the amount to transfer’, ensure ‘2’ is entered. In ‘Step 3: Select Location (Turn-in clean rags)’, Select ‘Mark as Dirty’. TCMax® will say “Transferred” and you will notice the Multi-item box shows “Sent to Dirty Rags”. ➤ If you select close and leave this screen you will notice the User no longer has Rags Issued to them. If you look at Issued Items, by going to the ‘Show Issued Items’ screen from the Top Toolbar or selecting the ‘Issued Items List’ at the bottom right-hand corner of the Main Screen, you will notice the Username is no longer specific to that User it states ‘Dirty Rags’. Press ‘Esc’ to clear the Main Screen if anything is displayed. Type ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® will say “Make Selection”. Select the column to the left of the Rags to highlight the 2 that are Marked Dirty. ➤ You will notice in Step 2 that a quantity of 2 is auto populated by highlighting the row. In ‘Step 3: Select Location (Turn-in clean rags)’, Select ‘Send to Laundry’, TCMax® will say “Transferred” and you will see ‘Sent to Laundry’ appear in the Multi-Item box. Close the Multi-Item box and navigate to the ‘Issued Items List’ from the bottom right-hand corner of the Main Screen or the ‘Show Issued Items’ screen from the Top Toolbar. Once you have navigated to the ‘Issued Items’ screen, you will see that your Rags are still issued to ‘Dirty Rags’, but the Location has adjusted to ‘Laundry’. With the Main Screen cleared, type in ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® will say “Make Selection”. Select the column to the left of the Rags to highlight the 2 that are being Returned. ➤ You will notice in Step 2 that a quantity of 2 is auto populated by highlighting the row. In ‘Step 3: Select Location (Turn-in clean rags)’, Select ‘Turn-In and Close’, TCMax® will say “Turn-In”. ➤ The Rags are now turned back into inventory. You will notice your ‘Quantity Available’ has adjusted accordingly. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Item Search will display your Items based on your Search Options, if you enter criteria into the Search Fields it will narrow down your search. The Search Fields are ‘AND’ not ‘OR’. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Item Search’. In the ‘Item Name box’, type ‘Wrench’, and press the ‘Enter’ key. Notice TCMax® now shows only items with ‘Wrench’ in the name. Press the ‘Close’ button.

info By default, you're not required to have a user or work location displayed to turn items in. Type ‘003’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Turn In”. Type ‘005’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Turn In”.

info The Kit Builder screen helps you quickly build, modify, and duplicate kits or toolboxes. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Tools’ then select ‘Kit Builder’ or press ‘Ctrl-K’ on your keyboard from the Main Screen to open the Kit Builder screen. Under Kit Shop Code, select ‘TCMax® Demo Shop’. Under Enter Kit Id, enter ‘600’ then press the ‘Enter’ key or press ‘Load Kit’. ➤ You will see your Kit displayed under the Kit Layout section. Once your Kit is displayed you can adjust Storage Locations, Remove Items, Add or Duplicate Items, and View the Selected Item’s Details. Click ‘Clear Display’. Under ‘Enter’ Kit Id, press ‘Create New Kit’. Under Barcode Id, enter ‘400’. Now you will be able to type in an Item Name, Storage Location, NSN, Part Number, and Serial Number for the Kit. After the information is entered, press ‘Save’. ➤ You will now see your Kit displayed under the Kit Layout section. Once your Kit is displayed you can Add, Move, or Duplicate Items from Inventory, Create New Items, Adjust the Storage Location, and View the Selected Item’s Details. Close the Kit Builder screen by pressing the ‘Close’ button or the ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner.

info A Maintenance Procedure is a specific task within an organization that requires a certain set of items and equipment to perform. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Tools’ then select ‘Maintenance Procedure / Bulk Issue Setup’. Ensure the Tire Change List – 807 is selected under ‘Select Maintenance Procedure’. Under ‘Add Item to Maintenance Procedure’, type ‘111’ and press the ‘Enter’ key. Under ‘Add Item to Maintenance Procedure’, type ‘114’ and press the ‘Enter’ key. ➤ Notice we are typing in Barcode Id Numbers, but the Part Numbers are displaying. This is because TCMax® associates Maintenance Procedures with Part Numbers. Therefore assets that are added to a maintenance procedures must have a Part Number. Close the Maintenance Procedures / Bulk Issues Setup screen by pressing the ‘Close’ button or the ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner. On the Main Screen of TCMax®, type ‘807’ then press the ‘Enter’ key. The Maintenance Procedure will print as long as a receipt printer is assigned and show where the item is located or who has the item issued and where.

info The Options screen will display all of the built-in Options within TCMax®. You can select or deselect Options depending on how you want TCMax® to operate on the Local Machine. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Settings’ then select ‘Options’. ➤ Notice the 5 (five) different tabs starting with ‘General Options’ at the top of the screen. These tabs are preloaded with over 140+ built in Options. Once adjusting the Options you wish to have selected within TCMax®, press ‘Save’ in the bottom right-hand corner.

info Reports from the Top Toolbar will display built-in Reports within TCMax® and are designed to help you review your data and organize the different historical events. info Each user can be assigned independent permissions depending on their role within the software. Below will outline how to set special access permissions for a User. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Settings’ then select ‘User Options’. Display a User from the User Permissions tab. Type ‘03’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 1200’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘111’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. ➤ Let’s look to see who has what. Press ‘Ctrl+S’ this brings up the Issued Items grid to the right of the screen. Press ‘Ctrl+S’ to exit Issued Items and returns to Item Details. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Show Issued Items’ or press ‘Ctrl+I’. The list of items currently issued appears. Notice you can mark any item in this list as Broken, Unserviceable, Lost, or Long Term. Close the Show Issued Items screen.

info A video walkthrough is available for this process here. tip It is recommended that you reach out to TCMax® Support Staff for assistance on migrating your Data To begin migration you will want to have TCMax® Version 9 installed and licensed on your destination computer as well as your Version 8.10 Microsoft® Access Database (if standalone) or access to the Microsoft SQL Server®. note If you are running 8.9 or earlier you must first upgrade to 8.10.590.

Within TCMax® Version 9, navigate to File > Import / Export Records. We can migrate Data from both Microsoft SQL Server® and Microsoft® Access Databases. Therefore, the remainder of this outline is split up into two categories, Migrating your Data from a Microsoft SQL Server® and Migrating your Data from a Microsoft® Access Database.

If your Version 8 Data is in a Microsoft SQL Server® Database, select the SQL Server radio button and then click the Set Source button which will bring up a Connections Properties window. Enter your Server Name, Authentication Method, and Database. Click the Test Connection button and if it says “Test connection succeeded” you can click OK to proceed. If it gives any result other than “Test connection succeeded.” take note of the error indicated and correct the connection information. When finished select OK. Select the Set Destination button and follow the same steps, except in this case you will enter the destination server’s information. When finished select OK.

To verify that your source Database is up to date and all datatypes are correct you will need to select the Verify Source Database button. This step is not optional and must be completed before progressing to step two.

Once your Database has been verified, select the Sync Data button to move the Data into your destination SQL Server Database. During the sync, information will appear on the screen letting you know what step of the syncing process you are on.

You can remove any old Database tables that will no longer be used by TCMax® by clicking the Remove Old Data button. By opting to leave Old Data, you will notice all the Version 8 tables will still remain intact but will essentially be 'archived' Data from the migration point.

Your Data should now be migrated and by re-establishing your TCMax® connection to the destination server you should see all your Data available. note Often times, unless the destination server Database was empty you will need to enable the new Shop Code within Settings > Sites and Shops.

note If migrating a standalone Database (Microsoft® Access), you will need to be on TCMax® version 9.8.7802 or older. This feature is removed due to deprecated Microsoft Software. If you are using a newer version of TCMax®, contact the Soaring Software Solutions support office for assistance. If you are using a Microsoft® Access Database, select the Access radio button then select the Set Source button to bring up a File Explorer window that can be used to navigate to your Microsoft® Access Database. Ensure your Microsoft® Access Database is local to this computer's hard drive and not on a media or networked location. Locate and select your Microsoft® Access Database and press Open. Set your destination Database by selecting Set Destination or by leaving this default, your Data will be migrated into the currently established connection (the Database you are working in). After you have chosen your Microsoft® Access Database and your destination Microsoft® SQL Database proceed to the next step.

This process requires you to have SQL Server Migration Assistant (SSMA) installed on your computer and also requires some form of the Microsoft® Access Database Engine. By selecting the Transfer Access Database button, TCMax® will launch a command line window which will pause early on and prompt you (indicated green) to enter a password for the Microsoft® Access Database. When prompted, enter the Database password and press Enter on the keyboard. The default Database password is Servic1. Once the password has been entered the query execution will resume and may take some time. If there are no issues you will be taken back to the migration window and may proceed to the next step.
documents.s: Prerequisite: Transfer Access Database to SQL Server

documents.t: Once SSMA has moved all of your old Version 8 Microsoft® Access Data into temporary tables in your new Database, select the Verify Source Database button which will verify the old Microsoft® Access Data is complete and ready to be synchronized.

Select the Sync Data button to move the Data to your Microsoft® SQL Server Database. During the sync process, you will provide input to different prompts, outlined below. Tool Chits Migration​ Select Shop Code​ Migrate Special Options Data​ This window is used to let us know how the Data needs to be copied based off of the options you were using in Version 8 of TCMax®. Select the Shop Code(s) that you would like to run the tool against and click the Migrate button under the Special Options that you were using. Once this is finished you can select the Close button to close this window and return to Migration screen.

You can remove any old Database tables that will no longer be used by TCMax® by clicking the Remove Old Data button. By opting to leave Old Data, you will notice all the version 8 tables will still remain intact but will essentially be 'archived' Data from the migration point.
You can now select Close and verify your items have migrated to your destination Database. note Often times, you will need to select the new Shop Code within Settings > Sites and Shops.
